classification.classification_note: The dataset description points at missing minimum-length checks around `strncmp`. The saved AddressSanitizer symptom is `negative-size-param` because the later trailer builder subtracts 5 from `strlen(param->armorhdr)` after that parsing logic has admitted an empty armor header. The resulting `memcpy()` would read from `param->armorhdr + 5`, four bytes past a 1-byte heap allocation.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists due to missing checks on string lengths when using strncmp for minimum bounds.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 34-byte witness is a malformed ASCII-armored PGP blob whose first 10 bytes are all `'-'`, whose later bytes contain the substring `-----BEGIN PGP `, and whose remaining body is just a blank line plus checksum line `=azaS`. In vulnerable `src/librepgp/stream-armor.cpp`, `stream_dump_packets()` treats the input as armored and `armor_parse_header()` calls `find_armor_header()`. That helper records the first five dashes at bytes 0..4 as the opening delimiter and then reuses bytes 5..9 of the same 10-dash run as the closing delimiter, so it reports `armhdrlen == 10` and leaves an empty interior string of length `armhdrlen - 10 == 0`. `armor_str_to_data_type()` then uses `strncmp(..., len)` with that attacker-derived zero length, so the empty string matches `"BEGIN PGP MESSAGE"` and is accepted as a valid armored message type. `armor_parse_header()` allocates `armhdrlen - 9 == 1` byte for `param->armorhdr` and materializes it as the empty string. On the first read after header parsing, the remaining line `=azaS` is treated as checksum/trailer input, so `armored_src_read()` calls `armor_read_trailer()` with `param->armorhdr == ""`. There `stlen = strlen(param->armorhdr)` is 0, the guard checks only `stlen + 8 + 1 <= sizeof(st)`, and `memcpy(st + 8, param->armorhdr + 5, stlen - 5)` underflows the size argument to `(size_t)-5`. AddressSanitizer reports `negative-size-param (size=-5)` at `armor_read_trailer` line 201. The fix both requires exact armor-header string lengths and adds the missing `stlen > 5` obligation before constructing the expected trailer.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the malformed armor header on the crashing path. This loop turns the staged leading dash run into a concrete candidate header length and pointer that later drive both type classification and `param->armorhdr` allocation.
source.value_from:
The staged `poc` is exactly `----------
-----BEGIN PGP 

=azaS
`. While `armor_parse_header()` scans it, the opening-dash search has already recorded `st = 0` on bytes 0..4 of the leading `----------`, and this loop then matches another `-----` immediately at `i = 5` on bytes 5..9 of that same run. It therefore returns a candidate header spanning bytes `[0,10)` and sets `armhdrlen = 10`, leaving an empty interior string of length `armhdrlen - 10 == 0`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This sequence materializes the attacker-derived header name as heap object `param->armorhdr`. With `armhdrlen == 10`, it allocates a 1-byte buffer, copies zero bytes into it, and stores a terminator, producing the empty string later measured by `strlen()` and indexed by `+5` in the crashing trailer copy.

root_cause.description: Incomplete minimum-length check. This guard validates only that the reconstructed trailer would fit in stack buffer `st`; it does not require `stlen > 5` before the next statement uses `param->armorhdr + 5` and `stlen - 5`. The fix changes this exact predicate to `(stlen > 5) && (stlen + 8 + 1 <= sizeof(st))`.

sink.description: ASan sink. With `stlen == 0`, the copy length underflows to `(size_t)-5`, and the source pointer `param->armorhdr + 5` points four bytes past the 1-byte allocation created in `armor_parse_header()`. AddressSanitizer aborts at this call with `negative-size-param (size=-5)`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged bytes at offsets 11..25 contain the exact substring `-----BEGIN PGP `, so `is_armored_source()` returns true and `stream_dump_packets()` enters the armored-input path by calling `init_armored_src()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The packet dumper recognizes the staged witness as armored input because it contains `-----BEGIN PGP ` and dispatches into `init_armored_src()`.
Header parsing turns the leading 10 dashes into a zero-length armor header, accepts that empty name as `PGP_ARMORED_MESSAGE`, and stores `param->armorhdr` as an empty heap string.
Because the remaining body is only the checksum line `=azaS`, the first read takes the immediate CRC/trailer path without decoding payload bytes and enters `armor_read_trailer()`.
`strlen(param->armorhdr)` yields 0, the stack-size guard omits the required `stlen > 5` check, and `memcpy(..., stlen - 5)` underflows to the saved AddressSanitizer `negative-size-param` at line 201.

fine_trace.note: While `armor_parse_header()` scans the staged prefix, the first loop has already recorded `st = 0` on bytes 0..4 of the leading `----------`. This second loop then finds another `-----` immediately at `i = 5` on bytes 5..9 of the same run, so it returns a candidate header spanning only those ten dashes and sets `*hdrlen = 10`. The interior name slice that later becomes `armhdr + 5` therefore has length 0.

`armor_parse_header()` calls this helper with `str = armhdr + 5` and `len = armhdrlen - 10 = 0` from step 1. `strncmp(..., 0)` compares zero bytes and returns 0, so the empty interior is accepted as `PGP_ARMORED_MESSAGE` instead of being rejected as `PGP_ARMORED_UNKNOWN`.

With `armhdrlen == 10`, the allocation size `armhdrlen - 9` is 1 byte, the copy length `armhdrlen - 10` is 0, and the terminator write leaves `param->armorhdr` as the empty string `""`. The saved ASan allocation stack names `armor_parse_header` line 565 and reports a 1-byte heap region, matching this exact state.

On the first `src_eof()` probe after header parsing, `armored_src_read()` sees the remaining line `=azaS` and takes its checksum/trailer branch immediately: `armor_read_padding()` treats a 5-character line as 'no padding', `armor_read_crc()` consumes `=azaS`, and `armor_read_trailer()` is entered without any decoded payload bytes. Here `param->armorhdr` is still the empty string from step 3, so `strlen` sets `stlen = 0`.

The only trailer-construction guard validates stack buffer capacity, not the minimum source-header length. Because `0 + 8 + 1 <= 64` is true, the function continues even though the next copy uses `param->armorhdr + 5` and `stlen - 5`. The fix strengthens this exact condition to `(stlen > 5) && ...`.

Sink. Reusing step 4's `stlen == 0`, the third argument underflows to `(size_t)-5` and the second argument points four bytes past the 1-byte `param->armorhdr` allocation from step 3. AddressSanitizer intercepts this `memcpy` as `negative-size-param (size=-5)` at `armor_read_trailer` line 201.

poc.trigger: The saved Stage 01 command runs `docker exec gt-arvo_24528-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` on this exact file and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param (size=-5)` in `armor_read_trailer()`.

format.name: malformed ASCII-armor header with zero-length name
format.contract:
Exactly the 34-byte witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_24528/poc`: `----------
-----BEGIN PGP 

=azaS
`. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to this observed layout: bytes 0..9 are ten consecutive dashes, bytes 11..25 contain `-----BEGIN PGP `, bytes 26..27 are a blank line, and bytes 28..32 are the checksum line `=azaS`. On the crashing path, `find_armor_header()` reuses bytes 5..9 of the leading dash run as the terminating delimiter, so `armhdrlen == 10`; `armor_str_to_data_type()` therefore receives a zero-length name, `param->armorhdr` becomes the empty string, and the checksum-only body immediately drives `armored_src_read()` into `armor_read_trailer()`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader malformed-armor contract beyond this witnessed zero-length-header and checksum-only layout.
